mutants.why: the PVD parse must select the type-1 Primary Volume Descriptor; inverting the guard makes the reader SKIP the real PVD (continue) and never fill any field, so the volume label is never read. analyzeReadsPrimaryVolumeDescriptorFields asserts QCOMPARE(info.volume_label, QStringLiteral("SAK_TEST_VOL"))

the Volume Identifier field starts at PVD offset 40; reading one byte late decodes "AK_TEST_VOL" instead of "SAK_TEST_VOL", dropping the leading char and mis-decoding the identifier a Windows-vs-Linux match depends on. analyzeReadsPrimaryVolumeDescriptorFields asserts QCOMPARE(info.volume_label, QStringLiteral("SAK_TEST_VOL"))

the LE-32 Volume Space Size sits at PVD offset 80; a one-byte shift reads [81..84] = 0 for the synthetic image (little-endian value 20 -> 0), mis-decoding volume_size to 0. analyzeReadsPrimaryVolumeDescriptorFields asserts QCOMPARE(info.volume_size, static_cast<uint64_t>(kSyntheticSectors) * kSectorSize)

the UDF BEA01 identifier compare must MATCH exactly; flipping ==0 to !=0 makes every non-UDF sector satisfy the branch, so non-UDF junk is stamped as a UDF filesystem (fail-open). analyzeRejectsBytesThatAreNotIso9660 asserts QVERIFY(info.filesystem.isEmpty())

ISO 9660 is asserted only when a real PVD yielded a volume label; inverting makes a valid labelled ISO report an EMPTY filesystem (and would stamp label-less junk as ISO 9660). analyzeReadsPrimaryVolumeDescriptorFields asserts QCOMPARE(info.filesystem, QStringLiteral("ISO 9660"))

the El Torito scan must process the type-0 Boot Record; inverting != to == makes it CONTINUE past every boot record so the catalog is never read and is_bootable stays false. analyzeReadsElToritoBootTypeFromCatalog asserts QVERIFY(efi_info.is_bootable)

a zero catalog pointer means no bootable catalog; inverting the test routes a VALID non-zero pointer to Unknown/Invalid (never classifying the real catalog) so is_bootable becomes false. analyzeReadsElToritoBootTypeFromCatalog asserts QVERIFY(efi_info.is_bootable)

an image is bootable exactly when the catalog produced a recognized boot type (not Unknown/Invalid); inverting marks a "UEFI" catalog as non-bootable. analyzeReadsElToritoBootTypeFromCatalog asserts QVERIFY(efi_info.is_bootable)

the boot platform is the Validation Entry byte at catalog offset 1, not the Default Entry boot-indicator (0x88) at offset 32; reading offset 32 reintroduces the historical bug that classified every EFI image (0x88 != 0xEF) as Legacy BIOS. analyzeReadsElToritoBootTypeFromCatalog asserts QCOMPARE(efi_info.boot_type, QStringLiteral("UEFI"))

a full 2048-byte sector read is a success; a read caps at kSectorSize so > can never be true, making readSectorAt ALWAYS fail and classifyBootCatalog return Unknown/Invalid for every catalog. analyzeReadsElToritoBootTypeFromCatalog asserts QVERIFY(efi_info.is_bootable)

either an os_family of Windows OR non-empty editions must route to the Windows installer; requiring BOTH makes a Windows-family image with no parsed editions fail the check. windowsFamilyIsInstallMedia sets only os_family and asserts QVERIFY(IsoAnalyzer::isWindowsInstallMedia(info)) (windowsEditionsImplyInstallMedia kills the other operand)

os_family is set to Windows only when the label/application ID carry Windows metadata; inverting the early-return makes a real Windows image bail out before setting os_family (and would stamp Windows on non-Windows media). analyzeClassifiesSyntheticWindowsMediaFromLabel asserts QCOMPARE(info.os_family, QStringLiteral("Windows"))

the minimum-size guard rejects an image smaller than the 16-sector system area plus one full descriptor sector (kMinIsoSize); the smallest LEGAL image is EXACTLY kMinIsoSize, so the bound must be '<' (accept the boundary) not '<=' (reject it). Relaxing '<' to '<=' rejects a valid minimal ISO and makes analyze() return an empty IsoInfo, so the volume descriptors are never read. analyzeAcceptsImageExactlyAtMinimumSize feeds a 17-sector image sized exactly kMinIsoSize with a valid PVD and asserts QCOMPARE(info.volume_label, QStringLiteral("SAK_MIN_ISO"))

mutants.find: return;  // Not an ISO 9660 volume descriptor
mutants.replace: continue;  // Not an ISO 9660 volume descriptor
mutants.why: before decoding any PVD field the reader confirms the scanned sector carries the "CD001" standard identifier; a sector that lacks it means the descriptor set ended (or the media is corrupt) and the scan must STOP fail-closed. Turning the 'return' into 'continue' walks past the invalid sector and mis-decodes a Primary Volume Descriptor from unrelated later data, surfacing a bogus volume label analyze() must never report. analyzeStopsScanAtFirstNonDescriptorSector puts a non-descriptor sector at LBA 16 and a valid PVD at LBA 17 and asserts QVERIFY(info.volume_label.isEmpty())
